## _As an Environment Artist at OVFX Studios, Raghav brought breathtaking dome tents to life in his mentorship project at Think Tank Training Center._

* * *

# **Interview with Raghav Verma |**[**Swamp Haven**](https://www.artstation.com/artwork/n0R1g6)**| 3D Artist**

* * *

# **Artist Introduction**

Hey! My name is Raghav Verma, I’m currently working as an Environment Artist at the OVFX Studios for an unannounced Netflix and Hulu title. What can I say, I love to create things! Be it environment, props, or procedural systems for environments! My focus remains on game art which uses real-time rendering pipeline using game engines like Unreal Engine to create beautiful environments. I'm also a ThinkTankTraining Centre Alumni, and I’m known for my popular game environment project named [**_Swamp Haven_**](https://www.artstation.com/artwork/n0R1g6) which is my latest environment project.

# **Tell us about the project - Swamp Haven**

[** _Swamp Haven_**](https://www.artstation.com/artwork/n0R1g6) is my mentorship project which was made as a part of my final term at my art school, i.e. Think Tank Training Centre. It was an ambitious project that I took the responsibility of to finish in 4 months of time. It focused on pushing my technical skills to make high quality game assets.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/ce5a9c494bfd4670a43f35622293c0f3/images/83edc4f47c514b1eb442e678ab2db557%E6%B2%BC%E6%B3%BD%E5%9C%A3%E5%9C%B01.png)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/ce5a9c494bfd4670a43f35622293c0f3/images/a719e6e00f204852be5be8df2cf44ef5MainShot.jpg)

# **You used Marvelous Designer for cloth simulation of the tents. Why did you decide to use Marvelous Designer?**

Marvelous Designer is the best go to software for making real-time cloth simulations, especially ones that require a lot of manual art direction. The availability of GPU driven simulation is a big help when it comes to creating cloth simulations in a tight schedule. However it also features CPU simulations for more accurate sims. SwampHaven had to be completed in 4 months, and I had tasks every single day which needed to be done quickly, especially the Dome Tents. The Tents were a reimagined version of the concept art that I followed. They had to make physical sense for which I designed some ideas with my mentor Declan Hart. Finally a dome tent with modular cloth parts was the idea we landed up on. Marvelous Designer helped a ton while making the cloth sims because of its wide variety of tools that helped in making the sims quick and simple.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/ce5a9c494bfd4670a43f35622293c0f3/images/d3c53579e564440f80183d7e36b86666%E6%B2%BC%E6%B3%BD%E5%9C%A3%E5%9C%B01.png)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/ce5a9c494bfd4670a43f35622293c0f3/images/4f16e0d47a844633a1ea8fd20cad7d172_C.jpg)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/ce5a9c494bfd4670a43f35622293c0f3/images/0bd48bb1f0a34691add95ab23ada7663Tents_Unreal.jpg)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/ce5a9c494bfd4670a43f35622293c0f3/images/6cb0cbef9d4e4d589f94321fa6fec7b0%E6%B2%BC%E6%B3%BD%E5%9C%A3%E5%9C%B03.png)

# **Can you give us a quick overview of the different tools used in your pipeline to complete the tent creation?**

For the most part, Pinning tools and Measure tools were the most important tools which were used for my Dme Tents. The ability to create attachment curves at a collision mesh using ‘Attach to Measure’ and ‘Surface Measure’ helped the cloth to stick to my meshes properly. Furthermore, the ability to add ‘Pressure’ to the geometry paired with availability of different types of cloth types also helped a ton in art directing the look of the cloth simulation.

Furthermore these tools used my Unreal Engine shader system which allowed me to control different types of control on the texture, like the color, dirt spread etc. as shown below. 

# **What tips do you have for other artists using Marvelous Designer for environment art for games?**

For the limited time that I have used Marvelous Designer, I’d say it’s a great tool for making quick static meshes that require drapery or any type of cloth sim. Compared to other softwares, the UI is easy enough to grasp and the ability to play around with the cloth while it’s simulating in real time allows for greater control in art directing any cloth mesh. I’d recommend artists to check out Marvelous Designer for generating quick and detailed cloth sims for their project because of its easy to learn pipeline.

# **Are there any areas/ideas you would like to utilize Marvelous Designer in your future project?**

For future I’d like to explore Marvelous Designer for animated cloth sims on an animated actor/avatar. I’ve seen some cool showcases of cloth sims on characters which look amazing. I’d love to try that out.

# **How can you describe your overall experience of the use of the Marvelous Designer?**

Overall, Marvelous Designer offers a robust set of tools for doing cloth simulation quickly and efficiently. It helps in art directing cloth in many ways that helps both environment and character artists and is an amazing go to tool for simulations!

content:
## _Meet the 'Girl Student' by Bora Kim —a stunning blend of creativity and technology crafted using Marvelous Designer._

* * *

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/cc0033acedaa434fa1a41d1dfb90da93/images/209ce26ef56246f6ac195e84a40689ab%E5%A5%B3%E5%AD%A6%E7%94%9F1.jpg)

# **Interview with Bora Kim | Girl Student | 3D Artist**

* * *

# **Following our previous interview about your _Selfie Girl_ artwork, you've returned with another incredible piece. Could you share a bit about your latest work, 'Girl Student'?**

Hello, this is Bora Kim, and I'm delighted to be back. This time, the theme of my artwork is a girl sitting in a classroom after school. The idea began with a simple desire to create a character in a school uniform. I initially considered settings like a playground or park, but ultimately, I chose a classroom for its deeper sense of nostalgia and memories.

# **I understand that you're currently working as a character modeler, and with each piece, the background and prop details seem to be becoming more intricate. As the backgrounds become more detailed, they also encourage viewers to imagine the story behind the character. I'm curious if this is an intentional approach—do you work with the idea of how you'd like the audience to imagine the character's story?**

I believe many people have experienced the quietness of school after classes, the sense of relief after a day's work, and the anticipation for tomorrow. I hope that when people view this artwork, they don't just focus on the character but also find themselves reminiscing about their own childhood or feeling a sense of connection through the background and small props.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/cc0033acedaa434fa1a41d1dfb90da93/images/b353d6ef0f8f4af18e7f6046f9f5e4f5%E5%A5%B3%E5%AD%A6%E7%94%9F4.jpg)

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/cc0033acedaa434fa1a41d1dfb90da93/images/2ec2fcfa6f67478fab250edb22915954%E5%A5%B3%E5%AD%A6%E7%94%9F2.jpg)

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/cc0033acedaa434fa1a41d1dfb90da93/images/a6c138ca9f1449cb8709a9b7d4645463%E5%A5%B3%E5%AD%A6%E7%94%9F3.jpg)

# **From the character to the background, which aspects did you focus on while working on each element?**

Since the character is a student, I wanted to convey a sense of unadorned innocence, so I focused on features like light makeup, a comfortable oversized hoodie, and a neat school uniform. For the background, I emphasized recreating elements based on relatable memories, such as the wooden floor, curtains, fluorescent lights, wall colors, and the marble beneath the windows.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/cc0033acedaa434fa1a41d1dfb90da93/images/219fa3f1a90e46b8acc731d4d7fab0db6.jpg)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/cc0033acedaa434fa1a41d1dfb90da93/images/01f177a557944b8580ff9f8b50e50862%E5%A5%B3%E5%AD%A6%E7%94%9F2.jpg)

# **I'm curious to know which parts of your work were created using Marvelous Designer？**

I used Marvelous Designer for all aspects involving fabric, such as the character’s school uniform, ribbon, hoodie, hair tie, and even the clothes on the rabbit attached to the bag, as well as the curtains in the classroom. For the school uniform shirt, I started with a shirt from the Marvelous Designer library as the base, fitted it to the character's body, and then created and matched the vest and skirt. To form the pleats in the skirt, I drew lines for folds both inside and outside and adjusted the Fold Angle value to create the desired shape.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/cc0033acedaa434fa1a41d1dfb90da93/images/20798cdce0a64a1daf3689b4856ce3dc%E5%A5%B3%E5%AD%A6%E7%94%9F5.jpg)

The hoodie required creating a 2D pattern for the shoulders, arms, and underarms that was wider than expected to achieve the oversized fit. After completing the creation, I imported the rigged animation to set various poses. Finally, I fixed one side of the hoodie to drape off the shoulder, easing the restrictive feeling of the uniform.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/cc0033acedaa434fa1a41d1dfb90da93/images/f5167050129d4fdcb7099df763154d28%E5%A5%B3%E5%AD%A6%E7%94%9F6.jpg)

For the curtains in the background, I first created a rod that would act as the avatar, then hung the fabric on it. Adjusting the width of the curtains made it easier to form the pleats. After that, I used the Wind Controller to simulate the effect of the thin fabric fluttering in the breeze from the window. I set up the wind in the direction it would blow, adjusted the Strength to an appropriate value, and experimented with turbulence and frequency settings until I achieved the desired look.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/cc0033acedaa434fa1a41d1dfb90da93/images/b75fefe67437459a8b85af48edd18746%E5%A5%B3%E5%AD%A6%E7%94%9F8.jpg)

I also created and used various other simple props.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/cc0033acedaa434fa1a41d1dfb90da93/images/6a880c4f02024691b477d190fca8d62a10.jpg)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/cc0033acedaa434fa1a41d1dfb90da93/images/3fb19a6f94eb4f2d8a970637671d779012.jpg)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/cc0033acedaa434fa1a41d1dfb90da93/images/8da9a9ec60e447969e664b1598d2d3d4%E5%A5%B3%E5%AD%A6%E7%94%9F7.jpg)

# **Did you find any unique advantages of using Marvelous Designer during this project?**

One of the major advantages of Marvelous Designer is its ability to quickly run simulations and adjust folds when the character takes different poses or when the clothing design changes. This flexibility in correcting and exporting the folds is a significant strength. Additionally, I found it convenient to obtain a cleaned-up low-poly mesh through the ZBrush plugin.

# **If there was an impressive story during the project, could you share it?**

During this project, due to personal circumstances, the working period was extended. As the seasons changed, I adjusted the school uniform design from summer to autumn attire, eventually adding a hoodie. I also changed the hairstyle from a ponytail to a half-up style, and finally to a bob cut. Although the work seemed never-ending at times, step by step, it eventually came together. Even though I felt anxious as time passed, I gained valuable insights from the trial and error, making it a worthwhile experience.

Thank you for your interest in my work and for taking the time to read this.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/cc0033acedaa434fa1a41d1dfb90da93/images/c348616f2aee45e1a5612921477f76c513.jpg)

content_description: Explore the creative journey of Bora Kim as she unveils her latest 3D artwork, "Girl Student," a nostalgic homage to school life, crafted with precision using Marvelous Designer.

## _Step into the world of Shakespearean drama, King Lear. This piece meticulously recreates the intricate costumes and emotions of the iconic characters._

* * *

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/205ff9812f494f8eb8a1e46ee9196b61/images/c3f7bf108e7746c4b07bb988f5fa23d764a345e18f6542b5b5531a19d6dbfa23.png)

# **Interview with Chuying | King Lear | 3D Character Artist**

* * *

# **Artist Introduction**

Hello everyone, my name is Chu Ying, and I am a 3D modeling hobbyist. I came into contact with 3D production by chance, and my mentor is YangGuang, who is an amazing character artist.

# **Tell us about the project: King Lear**

This artwork is based on an oil painting by Edwin Austin Abbey. I was deeply attracted to it when I saw it for the first time. As I learned more, I found out that the painting depicted a scene from King Lear, which is one of my favorite stories, so based on that I decided to try to create it in 3D.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/205ff9812f494f8eb8a1e46ee9196b61/images/a531c46d36fa4023ba79c19c954d337db2bb9810c60844e2af81cb62a53c8f95.png)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/205ff9812f494f8eb8a1e46ee9196b61/images/db8fa0f1571e496ba65824606fadd8c3c11a10bd29eb4054814862e694359352.png)

For this artwork, before starting it, I have spent a lot of time to understand the historical background and creation period of this work, as well as collecting more reference images that fit their background story, to ensure that I have a basic understanding of what kind of garments and textures I need to make.

I will gather those collected reference images in PureRef, including the garments, trims, hairstyles, armor or weapons, or any other that makes my inspiration sparks.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/205ff9812f494f8eb8a1e46ee9196b61/images/8fdaefa00c684a00aa89d41ff430b5f84f62396f8d0a4ca580a6086c97ba6207.png)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/205ff9812f494f8eb8a1e46ee9196b61/images/b2326ce06bc34f7b926fca2aac3c2a8497c5a8a0cb1d47998a7d41de20e13af3.png)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/205ff9812f494f8eb8a1e46ee9196b61/images/1efd60e20bec422bafa13b01e386c110c779e54d92294447a8c0f662c6283599.png)

These are the mood boards that combine the reference images.

# **Why did you decide to use Marvelous Designer? How did it help you serve art direction?**

Since I need to simulate a lot of fabrics in this artwork, I chose Marvelous Designer after trying a lot of software because it can quickly iterate to help me realize the required clothing and very realistic folds.

In Marvelous Designer workflow, first of all, I will quickly create a prototype of the clothing I need.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/205ff9812f494f8eb8a1e46ee9196b61/images/35f852d2187d4876bbf8ed35534d57b73e0f0355db6c4974bfe602b0d1d70623.png)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/205ff9812f494f8eb8a1e46ee9196b61/images/c96fc510ec5442b288a408dc808d9cfdd2c8b086a2cc4575968976d76a0ef5d8.png)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/205ff9812f494f8eb8a1e46ee9196b61/images/49b28e885b0d41659e24b84aa1da88924039a716b39047a6af70bcc0355c77dc.png)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/205ff9812f494f8eb8a1e46ee9196b61/images/cc57ef924a1d48fca614952508b2e25f1ec4721acb114baf9b2b8f1905fa4666.png)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/205ff9812f494f8eb8a1e46ee9196b61/images/02e2918d68784eb3bbd6ab9ef284b3b4c0fd7e8a8a4845858e2cb12fa6a0d23f.png)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/205ff9812f494f8eb8a1e46ee9196b61/images/eca5093e2e6b4f498c35e17fffeac490ed32abd618d8491e85497a6ebb1f9931.png)

Then I will export the model in Marvelous Designer to Maya to make a simple .pos file, and then import it in Marvelous Designer to simulate the garment draping that follows the pose changing. I really like this function because it achieves very good results and does not require too many settings. It is very simple and easy to use.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/205ff9812f494f8eb8a1e46ee9196b61/images/82eb49b1eb424f5f85504fee9886990e8c88f90faa10434f9eabf9105119be56.png)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/205ff9812f494f8eb8a1e46ee9196b61/images/a1681bdc85754c3db407a3c2d5862839e7844e7af7e54492abb210a4c96676b6.png)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/205ff9812f494f8eb8a1e46ee9196b61/images/d784e3ad757943f2aff48dd4c532dfe7a6a5ad433c5b4c14a1d7fc84c6638248.png)

I’ve also used those powerful features in making the scene fabrics, Marvelous Designer brings me realistic and natural fabric effects. I highly recommend you to take a try. It will help you to enhance the realism of the garment and the efficiency of creating the artwork. It doesn't require knowing complex dynamics, it's really easy to use, just press the magic space bar, and it will help you achieve the effect you want.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/205ff9812f494f8eb8a1e46ee9196b61/images/b3c2df28c6684195b58904da061700fe139d746b08ed4a048afb3d6f9a3e27f2.png)

# **Can you give us a quick overview of the different tools used in your pipeline?**

I’ve used Maya, Zbrush, Substance 3D Painter and some other 3D software.

# **Can you elaborate on the challenges while you’re working on the project: King Lear?**

The biggest challenge is handling a huge amount of simulation of garment and fabric, and changing the pose of the avatar is another big challenge. But fortunately, Marvelous Designer helps me to solve those problems.

# **What tips do you have for other character artists using Marvelous Designer?**

Importing the OBJ file that you make from other 3D software as Garment is very helpful for us to create the garment quickly.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/205ff9812f494f8eb8a1e46ee9196b61/images/782849a9eef34836950acce73ddaf5464d851eeb6b0e4309a3dce8f96c8776d1.png)

And recording animation function is helpful for me to simulate the garments. I can load a pose file and have the garment transform according to the joints.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/205ff9812f494f8eb8a1e46ee9196b61/images/1a48258d84b346419298f4d5e6ee1dee4dbb705ae03049418c9857cd0f51a786.png)

When creating the bands or stripes, Pin tool helps me to fix those fabrics in the air. I highly recommend you to use the pin to do the knots or twist the bands.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/205ff9812f494f8eb8a1e46ee9196b61/images/bf32429142914c66982af371e840024bb2555980393f4a13b399043cc711222b.png)

And if you have fabric simulation needs for making the environment, you can definitely try Marvelous Designer, build up a simple pattern and see how it goes.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/205ff9812f494f8eb8a1e46ee9196b61/images/324a1574deaf4be3bbcb5c33e190ae8e9e7b49d60172486eafae540f8b7f0406.png)

There are lots of tips and tricks when you are using Marvelous Designer, I cannot list them all with several sentences. You can follow up the Youtube or Bilibili official channel of Marvelous Designer, there are lots of good tutorials or nice videos about it. I’ve learned a lot since I followed up with these accounts.

# **How can you describe your overall experience of the use of the Marvelous Designer?**

Using it makes me feel wonderful, Marvelous Designer is absolutely an outstanding 3D design tool, it’s easy to use. The workflow could be more efficient and I could adjust the garments quickly based on the effect. The UI is user-friendly and the fabric simulation is realistic. It is compatible with other 3D software and is an ideal tool for promoting digital clothing design. By using Marvelous Designer, the designer's creativity can be extended infinitely.

content:
## _Explore Cyber Folklore with Zhiyan Cai, where tradition meets technology. Discover how Asian folklore is reimagined through 3D art and cyberpunk aesthetics._

* * *

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/5108cab8a46549f4940ce0469f4249b3/images/a3f00b62ce874e2cb043256c9c079cb5Cyber_Folklore1.webp)

# **Interview with Zhiyan Cai | Cyber Folklore | 3D Artist**

* * *

# **Artist Introduction**

I am Zhiyan Cai, a 3D artist and former architect currently residing in London. My work delves into the intricate relationships between culture and technology, history and the future. I enjoy intertwining Asian cultural elements with themes of futurism and science fiction, utilizing 3D rendering, parametric design, augmented reality, and virtual reality technologies to create visually immersive experiences that transcend traditional boundaries and spark imaginative journeys. My series "Cyber Folklore" has received enthusiastic acclaim on international design websites like Behance and Chinese design platform Zcool. My work has been showcased at prominent international art events, including Milan Design Week, London Design Festival, NYCxDesign, Design Shanghai, and Shenzhen Cultural Expo. Various domestic and international art media such as "Al-Tiba9 Art Magazine," "WWD China," and "Guoke Technology" have featured my pieces. My art embodies a romantic interpretation of mythology, regional culture, and science fiction. Despite being born in a modern metropolis, I frequently conduct art research in rural towns. Fascinated by various folk cultures, costumes, and legends, I view my creations as contemporary reinterpretations of myths, considering myths and legends as ancient forms of science fiction.

# **Tell us about the project - Cyber Folklore**

Cyber Folklore is a 3D visual art project that combines Asian cultural heritage with cyberpunk aesthetics. The inspiration for this project came from my research trips to places like Guizhou and Hunan in China. These regions are home to many Asian indigenous groups that showcase a rich diversity of cultural arts, including unique clothing designs, totems, embroidery, dance, and poetry.

In Cyber Folklore, I have reimagined various local folklore stories and mythical characters, with each piece depicting a different tale. The folklore is intertwined with visually striking sci-fi elements, creating a unique style that aims to bring cultural heritage into the realm of popular art.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/5108cab8a46549f4940ce0469f4249b3/images/8a39e577b94742c09c214eace5600802Cyber_Folklore2.webp)

# **Can you give us a quick overview of the different tools used in your pipeline?**

Clothing Modeling: Marvelous Designer

Texture Painting: Substance Painter

Character Models: Daz Studio

Animation: Cinema 4D

Rendering: Octane Render

# **Could you give examples of some of the iconic scenes and characters Marvelous Designer has been used for?**

Representative scenes in Cyber Folklore, such and "Miao," extensively use Marvelous Designer.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/5108cab8a46549f4940ce0469f4249b3/images/b294e48e19234d9ea4e88f1a15981f43Cyber_Folklore5.webp)

The inspiration for "Zhongkui" comes from the Fujian tradition of parading with large deity costumes during festivals, bringing blessings to the people. This iconic scene was also referenced in the famous sci-fi animation "Ghost in the Shell." The most stunning aspect of this scene in Cyber Folklore is Zhongkui's dramatic robe. I modeled this robe in Marvelous Designer, drawing heavily from the styles of Beijing opera costumes. In the scene, I wanted to convey not only the softness of the fabric but also the hardness and resilience of metal. To achieve this, I meticulously adjusted the physical parameters of the fabric simulation.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/5108cab8a46549f4940ce0469f4249b3/images/a74b74c48f414845adb96335dfe0353fCyber_Folklore7.webp)

Marvelous Designer also excels at simulating clothing animations. I created an animation of the character moving from an A-pose to walking, imported the character's Alembic file, and used the animation to simulate the clothing, outputting the Alembic clothing file. This file was then imported into Cinema 4D, where I used the Pose Morph Tag to link the existing clothing model, completing the animation rendering of the attire.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/5108cab8a46549f4940ce0469f4249b3/images/e3e38792cc844420b17907e920bad76ascreenshot4.webp)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/5108cab8a46549f4940ce0469f4249b3/images/ae9d5402256046f28d0e41c5bb0f7a48screenshot5.webp)

In the "Miao" scene, I aimed to showcase the intricate and luxurious beauty of Miao cultural attire. I took numerous photos at local folklore museums for reference, modeling each piece separately, including headscarves, skirts, belts, and shawls. The real-time simulation and rendering capabilities allowed me to ensure that the clothing perfectly fit the imported model's body.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/5108cab8a46549f4940ce0469f4249b3/images/992eecc6abd94ea094bff8904a8db59fscreenshot3.webp)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/5108cab8a46549f4940ce0469f4249b3/images/92804691412d4817846780068d84c0cbCyber_Folklore3.webp)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/5108cab8a46549f4940ce0469f4249b3/images/132b212d6f8e45c8959e508a860d14bcscreenshot2.webp)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/5108cab8a46549f4940ce0469f4249b3/images/89575111437e4024aa18f551847ad350Cyber_Folklore4.webp)

# **Can you elaborate on the challenges while you’re working on this project - Cyber Folklore?**

I don't have a professional background in fashion design, so I spent a lot of time studying the patterns of traditional costumes. Traditional opera costumes are structurally very complex, but fortunately, Marvelous Designer is very user-friendly and allows for easy modifications and re-simulations. By simplifying the complex patterns, I was able to quickly achieve the desired effect.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/5108cab8a46549f4940ce0469f4249b3/images/92c36cf18093418c8d280c219b30c4a4robe.webp)

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/5108cab8a46549f4940ce0469f4249b3/images/b2d53c7135424266a6eae03d919383d2flags.webp)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/5108cab8a46549f4940ce0469f4249b3/images/258b0f46be914ab3b273f770c5b8fa89screenshot1.webp)

Another challenge was the subtle adjustment of fabric textures. Many of the fabric effects I wanted were difficult to find in real life. Adjusting the Detail data in the Physical Property settings helped me achieve the desired look.

Additionally, I have always sought to explore the intersection of sci-fi and folk art in my aesthetics. I created mood boards while designing my characters and scenes, drawing inspiration from the stage performances and musicals of many renowned folk artists.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/5108cab8a46549f4940ce0469f4249b3/images/dd3ab4fc93094c4d8e76037e88a32b2dmood_board1.webp)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/5108cab8a46549f4940ce0469f4249b3/images/6dd60d4bee824fa5a9f1ffb69176667dmood_board2.webp)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/5108cab8a46549f4940ce0469f4249b3/images/09478a24321944ed88e463bad18279a9mood_board3.webp)

# **How can you describe your overall experience of the use of the Marvelous Designer?**

First of all, I believe that Marvelous Designer allows a non-professional in fashion like me to get started quickly due to its clear and simple interface. Using Marvelous Designer has also brought me a lot of inspiration. One of my previous projects, "Song of Spring," was an accidental creation while testing various features of the software. The design of my character's clothing was inspired by the attire of the Miao people. However, I also wanted to reflect the organic image of the Miao goddess "Butterfly Mother" as she flutters her wings and connects with nature. By repeatedly simulating the animation, I created the romantic symbolism of a butterfly spreading its wings to bring spring.

# **What's next in store for you?**

Earlier this year, I collaborated with dancers and musicians to create a digital art show in London that combined my 3D animations. I thoroughly enjoyed the process of cross-disciplinary collaboration with different artists, as it always brings a lot of inspiration. I hope to continue such attempts in the second half of the year and welcome interested dancers and musicians to contact me. Commercial collaborations are also welcome.

Another project I'm currently working on involves creating a character in Unreal Engine using the Metahuman system. I customized my character, redesigned the hairstyle, and used Marvelous Designer to create the clothing. This work will be part of "Cyber Folklore 2."

# **What advice do you have for other 3D artists who may just be starting their careers?**

Stay curious and keep learning the latest technologies. Always maintain your unique style and continue pursuing what you are passionate about.

For those just starting their careers in 3D art, my advice is to approach every project with a sense of curiosity and a willingness to learn. The field of 3D art is constantly evolving with new technologies and techniques, so staying updated is crucial. Additionally, it's important to develop and maintain your unique artistic voice. Your individual style is what will set you apart in the industry. Finally, never lose sight of what you love about your work. Pursuing your passions will keep you motivated and drive your creative journey.

content:
## _Just had the incredible opportunity to learn more about Simin (Simba) Farrokh Ahmadi's project - "Rhymes & Remedies.", a talented Props & Environments Artist⁠._

* * *

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/7cd50175928c4c7f9bc6c7862a22a671/images/bf8d3d43b7214333a815030eb28b8729ezgif-2-36f89a4cbe.webp)

[_Full video_](https://vimeo.com/950900935)

# **Interview with Simin (Simba) Farrokh Ahmadi | Rhymes & Remedies | Props & Environments Artist**

* * *

# **Artist Introduction**

Hello everyone! My name is Simin Farrokh Ahmadi, also known as Simba. I recently graduated in CG Asset Creation for Games at [Think Tank Training Centre](https://www.tttc.ca/), specializing in Props & Environments.

My journey as an artist began in my teenage years when I decided to study at an art conservatory instead of a conventional high school. This path led me to earn a national certificate in fine arts, a bachelor's degree in interior design, and a master’s degree in animation. With a background in architectural visualization, I felt something was missing in my life – the joy of creating visually stunning projects in real-time environments. So I took a leap of faith and left my job to learn new skills.

In January 2023, a life-changing event occurred when I was awarded the [Warner Bros. Discovery Access Canada ](https://www.linkedin.com/company/wbd-access-canada/)Doers and Dreamers Digital Art Scholarship to study at Think Tank Training Centre. This was a significant step toward realizing my dreams. “[Persian Afternoon](https://www.artstation.com/artwork/rJWJ05)”, “[A Day in Heaven](https://www.artstation.com/artwork/8bEzXQ)”, “[Silent Elegance](https://www.artstation.com/artwork/dKnvmW)”, and “[Rhymes & Remedies](https://www.artstation.com/artwork/PXAqX4)” are among the projects I created during the program.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/7cd50175928c4c7f9bc6c7862a22a671/images/f91c60827e0548919e395739b97c6b30_0001.jpg)

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/7cd50175928c4c7f9bc6c7862a22a671/images/7df91dd360da422eada53265a2a0d638_0002.jpg)

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/7cd50175928c4c7f9bc6c7862a22a671/images/5dbc252550da4e1aab7a6767375dcf22_0003.jpg)

# **Tell us about the project -Rhymes & Remedies.**

“Rhymes & Remedies” is my most personal project to date. Created as my mentorship project at Think Tank under the guidance of [Nikhil Kedige](https://www.artstation.com/nikhilkedige), it was inspired by an illustration by [Marlowe Lune](https://www.marlowelune.com/). The artwork evoked memories of my childhood library, a haven filled with books where I spent endless hours immersed in reading. My goal was to capture the cozy and safe feeling of that space while incorporating my dad’s poetry. This became the core goal of the project. Gradually, the project transformed into an homage to my parents, who have always encouraged and inspired my artistic journey. Although they have dedicated their careers to healthcare and saving lives, both my mom and dad are artists at heart. This project is a tribute to them and their spark of imagination that breathes life into my passion for art.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/7cd50175928c4c7f9bc6c7862a22a671/images/f9adf29f2f424d2cb0a5c63bca5b0e48_0004.jpg)

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/7cd50175928c4c7f9bc6c7862a22a671/images/a6d75d4ff439419c81cf171b53b8300e_0005.jpg)

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/7cd50175928c4c7f9bc6c7862a22a671/images/e95538fd3f7e4091ab3a48df2c27e304_0006.jpg)

# **In what ways did you use Marvelous Designer in your project?**

I used Marvelous Designer to create the main armchair, the tablecloth, and statue dress. I also used male and female avatars as base meshes for my statutes and busts.

# **What benefits did Marvelous Designer bring to your project?**

Creating realistic fabric folds and wrinkles is challenging in sculpting software, but Marvelous Designer significantly simplifies this process.

# **Can you give us a quick overview of the different tools used in your pipeline?**

Artists usually use Marvelous Designer to create clothing and drapery, but it has many handy tools for creating sofas and armchairs. I found a reference for a classic woodworked leather sofa that matched the style I had in mind and decided to recreate it.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/7cd50175928c4c7f9bc6c7862a22a671/images/3528d04339f341948dbd7f982b14dfa1_0007.jpg)

To create the armchair's fabric, I first made a low-poly structure in Maya and imported it into Marvelous Designer. I used the Flatten tool and selected the fabric mesh to get the pattern in the 2D window. While you can select all pieces and hit Enter, I personally find it more convenient to transform the fabric pieces one by one. This method allows for easier handling of potential errors.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/7cd50175928c4c7f9bc6c7862a22a671/images/0e748f57864542598f3746fd94ad254a_0008.jpg)

I then rearranged the 2D patterns to make them easier to work with. At this point I hid the wooden structure to work more conveniently.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/7cd50175928c4c7f9bc6c7862a22a671/images/f40be2fcd9e0449083726a3f86710c74_0009.jpg)

Using the Pin (Box) tool, I hovered over the edges of the fabric pieces. When a vertex turned blue, I double-clicked on it to pin the entire edge. After double-clicking, the pinned edge is marked with an orange line.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/7cd50175928c4c7f9bc6c7862a22a671/images/1a7d23ad4ee94f4094ca7af49ce29694_0010.jpg)

Next, using the Internal Polygon/ Line Tool, I started creating the internal sewn lines according to my reference. Then, I selected the internal lines with the Edit Pattern tool and Cut the lines.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/7cd50175928c4c7f9bc6c7862a22a671/images/e8ffa61daddf4c8e89e34a346ebeded0_0011.jpg)

This is how the patterns looked after all cuts and pins were in place. I tried to add a bit of randomness to the middle button pins so the wrinkles appear more natural.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/7cd50175928c4c7f9bc6c7862a22a671/images/866b18ba570944ae86aff34ca1ca3ec1_0012.jpg)

I used the Leather Fabric preset and adjusted a few parameters for Stretch and Weight. I then set Particle Distance to 5 mm and the Pressure to 10 to achieve the desired result.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/7cd50175928c4c7f9bc6c7862a22a671/images/b00336eedf8548509cf744c2b4ad3e2c_0013.jpg)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/7cd50175928c4c7f9bc6c7862a22a671/images/558cf610049646bf97ef3b09106ef26d_0014.jpg)

To create the tablecloth, I imported my table mesh as an avatar. I then drew a Rectangle in the 2D window, moved it above the table, and simulated it. I experimented a lot with the placement of folds while in simulation mode to achieve the desired effect.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/7cd50175928c4c7f9bc6c7862a22a671/images/393f009f66f54d94a2d90ffffa4493c9_0015.jpg)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/7cd50175928c4c7f9bc6c7862a22a671/images/556a5684e9984cc3b1dc43bb9d336aa0_0016.jpg)

For the female statue dress, I drew a Polygon, duplicated it, and then sewed the sides and strap together.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/7cd50175928c4c7f9bc6c7862a22a671/images/f71dc6d37d544c489a1ec2fa2bb32fd3_0017.jpg)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/7cd50175928c4c7f9bc6c7862a22a671/images/1a6c6a33ac1844cab6ed8403866c697d_0018.jpg)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/7cd50175928c4c7f9bc6c7862a22a671/images/6a290c366d8d4c7c912c4754e307ca82_0019.jpg)

I also used Marvelous Designer to create the suitcase lid compartment and fabric pieces around the room in my other project, “A Day in Heaven”.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/7cd50175928c4c7f9bc6c7862a22a671/images/859b29ee9eee4d369dcbd80cd2efe9f9_0020.jpg)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/7cd50175928c4c7f9bc6c7862a22a671/images/b31f59c10ef4495ebafb79986da036a6_0021.jpg)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/7cd50175928c4c7f9bc6c7862a22a671/images/9879b7a24a9a44d1a415a68f5a1a2c05_0022.jpg)

# **What tips do you have for other artists using Marvelous Designer for 3D Environment?**

Try experimenting with different presets and don’t be afraid to think outside the box. You might be surprised at how much you can achieve with Marvelous Designer, rather than spending hours sculpting from scratch.

# **How can you describe your overall experience of the use of the Marvelous Designer?**

It has been very rewarding actually! Marvelous Designer is a powerful tool with a very user-friendly UI. Once you get accustomed to how it works, you’ll likely want to use it as much as possible. I’m excited to explore and benefit from its various tools in my upcoming projects.

# **_by Simin Farrokh Ahmadi_**

content_description: Discover the creative journey of Simin (Simba) Farrokh Ahmadi as she shares insights into her heartfelt project "Rhymes & Remedies," blending artistry and personal inspiration in the realm of 3D prop and environment design.

title: The-Oyabun
content:
## _The Oyabun, which means 'the boss,' is the title of the leader in the Yakuza. Dive into the realistic character creation process using Marvelous Designer!_

* * *

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/8d831a43cad744d0b70714ceec27a27d/images/606877c5fdbb45fa9b016cc4c26d6272b1eb98dc47cf4c98b8e001c3ca3cb5ec.jpg)

# **Interview with****Xhon Hysenaj****|****The-Oyabun | 3D Artist**

* * *

# **Artist Introduction**

Hello, I’m Xhon Hysenaj, an Italian 3D artist based in London, I currently work as a freelancer and I'm specialized in character modeling and design.

# **How did you first get started in 3D?**

I first got started in 3D when I discovered my passion for digital art during high school. Initially, I was fascinated by video games and animated movies, which sparked my curiosity about how these incredible worlds and characters were created. I began experimenting with free 3D modeling software and online tutorials, dedicating countless hours to learning the basics. My journey truly began to take shape when I took a few online courses, which deepened my understanding and skills. Eventually, I started working on small freelance projects, gaining practical experience and refining my craft. This combination of self-study, formal education, and hands-on work paved the way for my career as a 3D artist.

# **Tell us about the project: The-Oyabun**

Earlier this year, I took a trip to Japan, and when I returned, I felt incredibly inspired. Additionally, my interest was fueled by watching many movies and playing numerous video games related to the Yakuza.

The Oyabun, which means "the boss," is the title of the leader in the Yakuza. I decided to create a Yakuza character because I've always been fascinated by Japanese art, from architecture to product design.

While planning the project, I knew a few things: first, the character had to be elderly to differentiate from my previous projects and to practice something new; second, I wanted to work without a single specific main reference. I aimed to give myself more creative freedom and see how this would impact my workflow.

# **Why did you decide to use Marvelous Designer? How did it help you serve art direction?**

From the early stages, I knew the clothes will be the heart of the project. Without a clear reference in mind, I needed a tool that offered flexibility and precision.

Marvelous Designer was the perfect choice for my pipeline because it allows for realistic cloth simulation and intricate detailing. Its versatility enabled me to quickly experiment with different fabric designs and most importantly with different poses, ensuring the final look aligned perfectly with the artistic direction I was looking for.

# **Can you give us a quick overview of the different tools used in your pipeline?**

# **Project Pipeline Breakdown**

# **Reference Collection**

The first step in my pipeline is using PureRef to gather references for each aspect of the creation: head, hair, clothing, pose, and accessories.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/8d831a43cad744d0b70714ceec27a27d/images/4d601f9ec21041de80c58b161326c71f0315d81c01af495ca9f9edaa3227f94f.png)

# **Initial Setup in Autodesk Maya**

Next, I jump into Autodesk Maya, where I use a preexisting body shape as a mannequin to define the character's height and body size, considering his age and the initial pose idea. I quickly pose the mannequin accordingly.

# **Head modeling**

Once the pose is ready, I start working on the head using Mudbox, ensuring the proportions are correct. I use Texturing XYZ during the sculpting process for high-quality pore-level detail maps. Once the sculpt is complete, I proceed with texturing in Substance Painter and create the hair using Maya XGen.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/8d831a43cad744d0b70714ceec27a27d/images/05b77d0dc8ec454182d583c5e43d47d480f9f0c2827c475a8d029f70d8f20b1d.png)

# **Clothing Creation in Marvelous Designer**

I then move to Marvelous Designer to create the clothes using the mannequin previously created. Given that the character is a boss, I opted for a formal look: coat, jacket, suit pants, waistcoat, shirt, and tie. My experience in fashion helps me comfortably work with fabric patterns in the 2D pattern window.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/8d831a43cad744d0b70714ceec27a27d/images/7c1a7a4c3c3c42dd9bdebcfec161e24fezgif-5-075afd2682.webp)

# **Retopology and Mesh Optimization**

After achieving the overall composition, I export the model for retopology, a crucial and time-consuming step to ensure the mesh is optimized. To achieve a decent result, there are several options ranging from handmade retopology to various plugins for Maya or external software.

I used a technique taught to me at CG Master Academy during my Character Creation for Films-Cinematics course, making some personal modifications for quicker use.

For this process, there are two steps:

# **1\. Export Simulated Mesh in Pose:**

First, I export the simulated mesh in pose, dividing each garment with a particle distance of 10 to ensure enough resolution from the simulation.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/8d831a43cad744d0b70714ceec27a27d/images/2173cf797913415283f18578b2ebf056fc5c3310aef940f88b87977dd81125bf.png)

# **2\. Export Flat Garments:**

Second, I export each garment by resetting the 2D arrangement. This way, I have each garment laid flat, making it easier to view for retopology while keeping the same UVs as the simulated ones.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/8d831a43cad744d0b70714ceec27a27d/images/7dc68b9b1b914308ae3384ac901f9329d10e679408084e58bc77968da6d6c73f.png)

Once the export is completed, I import the simulated clothing into Maya and the flat garments into ZBrush. I then use ZRemesher in ZBrush to quickly improve the topology of the mesh.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/8d831a43cad744d0b70714ceec27a27d/images/d3790236ac51481884bf986944beab2ceba2e2cf08d9442f88ed0c53b26071b0.png)

Afterward, I transfer attributes in Maya using the sample space to transfer the UVs from the flat garment (Marvelous Designer) to the ZRemeshed geometry. Then, I transfer the vertex positions to place the flat ZRemeshed geometry into the simulated one.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/8d831a43cad744d0b70714ceec27a27d/images/754a751f7da54273908f6e67b5760629418dcb24bc6d4dc0a4d00d5542f6ad8d.png)

Next, I manually fix any errors, add thickness, and work on the final version of the UV, keeping in mind the next steps ahead.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/8d831a43cad744d0b70714ceec27a27d/images/abfd5eb7b95644e99b29833d0bd93dffbbdb98cebbfc424cb82235acc7f9b7f4.png)

I then move to ZBrush for sculpting the clothing details like wrinkles, stitching, and small imperfections. After this, I export the displacement maps from ZBrush and export a decimated version of each garment for Substance Painter where needed.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/8d831a43cad744d0b70714ceec27a27d/images/27142a5414004bd7b353ec853666fd49ezgif-2-a1a695b4f1.webp)

# **Texturing and painting**

I used Substance Painter for this process. Since the character is wearing a clean suit, my main focus was on getting the colors and composition right.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/8d831a43cad744d0b70714ceec27a27d/images/92662f9a83734f35ae77ad334a445fe6ezgif-2-9e0b9e9652.webp)

# **Look Development and Final Adjustments**

In this phase, everything is assembled together in Autodesk Maya. It's crucial to maintain flexibility in the pipeline to be able to go back and forth in case something is off when you work on the final steps. I used Arnold for building shaders and setting up the lighting. Once the rendering was completed, I did some post-processing in Photoshop to fine-tune the colors and adjust the background.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/8d831a43cad744d0b70714ceec27a27d/images/e8fba057e7174670810ad681967d287a03488d7fdd7742769c1d6abf75da9174.png)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/8d831a43cad744d0b70714ceec27a27d/images/ce9fc2b5bfbd45e7b3246fcb4aae60fbfe525306461943868783375f0a009afb.png)

# **How can you describe your overall experience of the use of the Marvelous Designer?**

Marvelous Designer is changing the way artists approach clothing in 3D. Being able to work with organic materials with ease has helped me a lot. I believe that having a real-time view of how the clothes interact with your model is a game changer for artistic direction.

# **What's next in store for you?**

Right now, I'm focused on building a strong personal portfolio, including a character that I’m currently working on. I plan to expand my skill set by learning more advanced techniques and tools to create better characters. I'm also looking forward to collaborating with other artists and studios on larger-scale projects. Working with a team always brings new perspectives and ideas, which is very enriching. I’m very grateful to the marvelous designer team for the opportunity to share this project. You can view more of my work on my [**_Artstation_** ](https://www.artstation.com/xhonhysenaj)page and my [**_Instagram_**](https://www.instagram.com/xh.art).
content_description: Explore the fascinating world of character creation in 3D art, inspired by the Yakuza, through the innovative use of Marvelous Designer as shared by talented artist Xhon Hysenaj.

title: Selfie Girl
content:
## _Explore Bora's hyper-realistic artwork, where perfect folds and intricate details come to life, inviting you into a captivating world of imagination and creativity._

* * *

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/f685869281f04d8c8b5bf73bf0a6f34b/images/509c17b91637469bb53856928bec3a9020a69c735c7b47129cda974c7e70fb17.jpg)

# **Interview with Bora Kim | Selfie Girl | 3D Artist**

* * *

# **Could you briefly introduce yourself and explain how you started working in 3D art?**

Hello, my name is Bora Kim, and I am a 3D artist working at a gaming company. I've always loved graphics in games and videos since I was young, with a particular interest in game art. This naturally led me to study 3D art and eventually enter the gaming industry.

# **Could you describe a recent project you've worked on in detail?**

I strive to experiment with various new styles in my work. In my most recent project, I designed a female character deviating from the usual game style by using Marvelous Designer to create modern clothing. I took inspiration from fashion shows and various products to create the outfits.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/f685869281f04d8c8b5bf73bf0a6f34b/images/e73d6fa3463f41b096585a87a5f6d1c09b157cba959742689bf094ee08cb2499.jpg)

# **The details of your work are impressive. What efforts did you make to depict the realistic folds?**

The top the character is wearing has multiple folds on the front, unlike a regular shirt. I considered the spacing and creases of the folds and crafted it to show a shoulder-down style, ensuring the folds along the arm were aesthetically pleasing yet not too long.

For the skirt design, which is high-waisted and has few folds, I aimed to express the material and the folds created by the zigzag lacing up to the waist.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/f685869281f04d8c8b5bf73bf0a6f34b/images/ba70dbaf6b32462a8d42c7cf0a0904409bd7b6c7b2dc458580d4c1fe339e5312.jpg)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/f685869281f04d8c8b5bf73bf0a6f34b/images/600bccc4788146fe8f4a50aaf880a7013ef634029ecd471fb505f98016696371.jpg)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/f685869281f04d8c8b5bf73bf0a6f34b/images/0334a26bc0e943058b668c88a77b63abb731135be96f452fbe522dc6cb8dc682.jpg)

For the skirt design, which is high-waisted and has few folds, I aimed to express the material and the folds created by the zigzag lacing up to the waist.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/f685869281f04d8c8b5bf73bf0a6f34b/images/9c43e9ad59314c62b7438418c898688e2f65046c989d4dfb856233c8cc167700.jpg)

# **Why did you decide to use Marvelous Designer, and how has it helped with art direction?**

I first encountered Marvelous Designer around seven years ago while creating ribbons, curtains, and fabric movements for props. Even though these were simple tasks, I was very satisfied with how much faster and more intuitive it was compared to other cloth simulations I had used. Gradually, I started creating simpler garments like T-shirts and pants, and as I gained more experience, I found it easier to make clothes.

# **When working on a project, there are likely parts you enjoy the most and others that are challenging. Which stage of the process do you find the most enjoyable?**

While I enjoy the modeling process, I find the most fun in texturing. After finishing the modeling, imagining the final output, and experimenting with different colors and textures feels like painting on a blank canvas, which I find very enjoyable.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/f685869281f04d8c8b5bf73bf0a6f34b/images/13c3e120bb494277ae5223c8e1987b7cf6a7e41b4388450097b3379aaeda5617.jpg)

# **What is the most challenging aspect of your projects?**

The most challenging part is when the silhouette of the garment doesn't turn out as expected after applying the 2D patterns to the avatar. With each new clothing item I create, I realize there's still so much to learn as I continue researching and studying.

# **Lastly, do you have any advice for beginners starting in 3D art, whether career advice or mindset tips for creating artwork?**

In the beginning, there are many tools to learn and the workflow can seem complex, leading to a lot of contemplation. Even if you feel you're progressing slower than others, keep at it with enthusiasm and patience. If you continue creating with passion and step-by-step dedication, you will definitely see good results. Thank you.

# **_by Bora Kim_**

title: Dark Pictures Anthology
content:
## _A BAFTA-winning game studio, Supermassive Games showcased various character outfits in their games using Marvelous Designer._

* * *

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/b59b8f5f779e4b479877aa565e98404a/images/b63b10d7e5e64482a041ff72f976e369Amy_Cloak_Bust_1.webp)

# **Studio and Artist introduction**

Supermassive Games are a BAFTA-winning game studio founded in 2008, developing innovative storytelling games. They have released a number of successful titles and are best known for the critically acclaimed PS4 hit Until Dawn, The Dark Pictures Anthology - a series of stand-alone, horror games - and teen-horror game The Quarry. Their most recent releases are The Devil in Me - the season one finale of The Dark Pictures - and Switchback VR on PS VR2.

# **Andor Kollar (Senior Character Artist)**

As a character artist at Supermassive Games, I use Marvelous Designer in the character creation pipeline. Marvelous Designer has been a very useful tool for The Dark Pictures Anthology. It can simulate beautiful clothing with realistic creases. In this article, I'd like to show you some character examples from the **Little Hope** and **The Devil** in Me games.

# **How is Marvelous Designer integrated into the project pipeline? Could you explain your workflow for making the assets Unreal Engine-ready?**

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/b59b8f5f779e4b479877aa565e98404a/images/8f743392894340eaaea305fc3bf61b25Andrew_Full-Body_1.webp)

**_Andrew – Little Hope_**

I usually focus first on Marvelous Designer to help create the base of the cloth, then I manually add the small details.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/b59b8f5f779e4b479877aa565e98404a/images/5b49fe61675f4186974f92eeadd7bfafAndrew_MarvelousDesigner%20v.1.png)

The base of the detailed ZBrush mesh is the simulated hoodie in Marvelous Designer.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/b59b8f5f779e4b479877aa565e98404a/images/57266e7b6ac84cccb2d1caaa8e63cc11Andrew_Hoodie_ZBrush.webp)

The final character in Unreal Engine.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/b59b8f5f779e4b479877aa565e98404a/images/d64b8d7a9e344966960a0b27b18f10f7Andrew_Hoodie%20v.1.png)

* * *

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/b59b8f5f779e4b479877aa565e98404a/images/e6c891db484849ca89f908e8fc1f99beMary_Cloak_Full-Body_2.webp)

**_Mary – Little Hope_**

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/b59b8f5f779e4b479877aa565e98404a/images/7ea2214d868c45eda513be38dfe10db7Mary_Marvelous-Designer_2.webp)

Mary has a character variant with a cloak. I used the standard Mary character as an avatar. 

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/b59b8f5f779e4b479877aa565e98404a/images/8f437d1101bb4fda8563bedc7103d7f4Mary_Marvelous-Designer_1.webp)

(I did these characters in an older version of Marvelous Designer. The new version has more tools for retopology which could now be used instead.) It is crucial that the final game mesh should have a proper clean edge flow which supports the rigging and future in-game cloth simulation. Here I show what I found to be one of the best workflows to achieve this. Marvelous Designer is based on sewing patterns like the work of a real tailor, which increases the realism if the pattern is correct. The UV should be the same as in the pattern editor, and it is important to export an unwelded geometry without thickness in real-world scale.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/b59b8f5f779e4b479877aa565e98404a/images/c4f3ec9350b649eb9b53b16dd2db2dfcMarvelous-Designer_Retopology_1.webp)

I am using the Couture tool for the retopology process. The final geometry is very clean, maintaining the shape of the cloth which was simulated in Marvelous Designer. 

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/b59b8f5f779e4b479877aa565e98404a/images/c6ef6622d1854d67bb13fb09b3907e70Marvelous-Designer_Retopology_3.webp)

Using ZRemesher on the 3d mesh could be good in certain cases, but I can make a cleaner edge flow if I use UV based mesh for the retopology instead of this. 

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/b59b8f5f779e4b479877aa565e98404a/images/03f11967b98e485c8191fbd0c6fed912Marvelous-Designer_Retopology_2.webp)

I make a flat UV based mesh with Couture, then I can use ZBrush or Maya to create a very clean retopology. 

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/b59b8f5f779e4b479877aa565e98404a/images/775454b6201b45949801d9d310934daaMarvelous-Designer_Retopology_4.webp)

I wrap the retopologized flat geometry with Couture to the 3d mesh. So finally, I have the same shape as the simulated cloth and the same UV as the Marvelous Designer sewing pattern, just with clean geometry.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/b59b8f5f779e4b479877aa565e98404a/images/c5aa7077f0d54f3dae96b7b19e4ae926Marvelous-Designer_Retopology_5.webp)

After the mesh is cleaned up, I make some additional sculpting and this is the detailed ZBrush mesh.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/b59b8f5f779e4b479877aa565e98404a/images/308cbd074cb64df6a15d8dbae549532eMary_Cloak_ZBrush_3.webp)

Marvelous Designer is also useful for creating realistic knots. Understanding the shapes is important, so I think it increases the realism if I follow how the cloth would behave in real life. I find it helpful to use the red pinpoints to create the desired shape. 

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/b59b8f5f779e4b479877aa565e98404a/images/4d8b98e8570241d1b69fbc55535b50abMary_Ribbon%20v%2C1.png)

* * *

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/b59b8f5f779e4b479877aa565e98404a/images/3fd30ccba3c64cf8a894b22633f43f0eAmy_Cloak_Full-Body.webp)

**_Amy – Little Hope_**

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/b59b8f5f779e4b479877aa565e98404a/images/04a0c30a769343928fb88d29bc94b744EMMA%20%EC%9A%94%EC%B2%AD%201%20v.1.png)

Marvelous Designer was extremely useful for making the medieval costume and the hood.

Finally, the game mesh has very clean geometry, which is important for nice texturing, rigging and possible in-game cloth simulation. 

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/b59b8f5f779e4b479877aa565e98404a/images/1664bded311949d3ac449b29b1af2e12Amy_Wireframe_2.webp)

* * *

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/b59b8f5f779e4b479877aa565e98404a/images/427c3fe74cb04e27b91b02bf327f2093Anthony_Full-Body_1.webp)

**_Anthony – Little Hope_**

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/b59b8f5f779e4b479877aa565e98404a/images/37cf593001654473b16bc2846e3a27e5Andrew_Trowsers%20v.1.png)

Marvelous Designer gave me a good base for this character.

* * *

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/b59b8f5f779e4b479877aa565e98404a/images/70a8d5c1b0e74b5c9e7fc4a18a456339Erin_Full-Body_1.webp)

**_Erin – The Devil in Me_**

I used a lot of red pinpoints for the rolled up sleeve of Erin’s jumper. 

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/b59b8f5f779e4b479877aa565e98404a/images/414c96c12c874953aea01799c272af87Erin_Marvelous-Designer_1.webp)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/b59b8f5f779e4b479877aa565e98404a/images/4931c6d4547642c8ac41e436b9dac040Erin_Jumper_2.webp)

Erin’s skirt is a good example, where if my UV follows the Marvelous Designer sewing pattern exactly, then I can easily add a striped fabric without distortion and stretching – exactly as it would be for the real fabric. 

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/b59b8f5f779e4b479877aa565e98404a/images/9a5bdf1ff8c94928a2bda476336afa31Erin_Kirt%20v.1.png)

Making the leather jacket, I simulated only the creases on the sleeves of the jacket. I wanted to get certain diamond shaped creases which is why I used many pin points. 

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/b59b8f5f779e4b479877aa565e98404a/images/bd9a4a76f44b4edcb92b74b1fd930d6fErin_Marvelous-Designer_2%20%281%29.webp)

I made a clean high poly mesh in Maya as the base of the low poly game mesh, so I did not need to use retopology in this case. I projected the Marvelous Designer cloth manually in ZBrush with the ZProject brush. 

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/b59b8f5f779e4b479877aa565e98404a/images/5152a971736d4a538372c7a18e2399bcErin_Jacket_Maya.webp)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/b59b8f5f779e4b479877aa565e98404a/images/1e342fe016914c05a7e1443d0fe1d450Erin_Jacket_ZBrush.webp)

This is the result in Unreal Engine.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/b59b8f5f779e4b479877aa565e98404a/images/f258b5204d7d46c38e53d005d1c10c37Erin_Jacket_1.webp)

**_Animatronic Patient – The Devil in Me_**

* * *

Sometimes I use more collision objects for the simulation and not only the human body itself. I created the gown in A-pose in Marvelous Designer, but for realistic cloth simulation, I animated the sitting character to the chair together with the cloth. To achieve this, I imported the FBX animation into Marvelous Designer.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/b59b8f5f779e4b479877aa565e98404a/images/1df2bf79d07b490280a50a989b99dfe0EMMA%20%EC%9A%94%EC%B2%AD%202%20v.1.png)

# **Which features do you want to see from Marvelous Designer in the future version?**

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/b59b8f5f779e4b479877aa565e98404a/images/ea55a1a7587e4a948fece56d151ea133Marvelous-Designer_Presets.webp)

I see it as a great user-friendly thing that we finally have a cloth library with example images, but I think it would be really useful if Marvelous Designer had more and better physical property presets (wool, jeans, silk, leather, cotton…). 

I have one of the best desktop CPU on the market (i9-13900K), but unfortunately Marvelous Designer is using only 10-40% of my CPU when I change the particle distance, or I simulate the cloth. The GPU simulation is quite fast, but it would be good to get a better core optimization for the CPU. 

# **Which advice would you give to users who are just beginning to use the software?**

I think Marvelous Designer is very user-friendly software that is easy to learn. But the majority of character artists are not tailors, so I recommend studying how real sewing patterns look and understanding their logic to get a proper cloth simulation. I think Marvelous Designer asset store is also useful because we can learn how others make certain clothes. I also recommend watching a lot of Marvelous Designer tutorial videos.
content_description: Explore the innovative use of Marvelous Designer in character outfit creation at Supermassive Games, renowned for their BAFTA-winning titles, showcasing the intersection of cutting-edge technology and artistic storytelling.

## _The Intro, a 3D visual designer specializing in 3D visual and motion design, showcased some truly iconic visuals in the project._

* * *

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/83f3baeea7cc4419b9bc0ee9d60b3dc6/images/f79ba960850c4e6fb6ee1df3ed6af6cc6a700437303d448b863545a0889630a7.jpg)

# **We'd like to learn more about you. Can you introduce yourself?**

Hello everyone, I'm The Intro, a working 3D visual designer, specializing in 3D visual design and motion design, the works I publish online are all done by me independently, including some work projects and daily practice works.

# **Tell us about your project - Virtual fashion.**

For the project Virtual fashion, the initial intention was because I needed to create some virtual digital human costumes for my daily work projects, and at that time I was very obsessed with virtual costume related works, so I wanted to create a complete set of works to improve my skills in this area.

I would check relevant information and a lot of references on the Internet before production, and then determine the style of the costume according to the theme I set, I usually use the time after work to create, about 3-4 days to complete a set of costumes and scene production and rendering.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/83f3baeea7cc4419b9bc0ee9d60b3dc6/images/8bf5610730574c0f8545d1e2843d95c4dfd7e0dd23744d4d8bd3d05291ddc4fb.png)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/83f3baeea7cc4419b9bc0ee9d60b3dc6/images/61df46f73c214ddabf41673e3540d95f2420dba154bf4a5e8c9246e439af925c.png)

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/83f3baeea7cc4419b9bc0ee9d60b3dc6/images/077f3a0298d44d219752bfc9f3bc9db43af8588e778e4ab4959451eda372d453.png)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/83f3baeea7cc4419b9bc0ee9d60b3dc6/images/04668b91d2fb4d998f7c97977cd06cb82b1ff53f88b145e597838d1517a5d0d4.png)

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/83f3baeea7cc4419b9bc0ee9d60b3dc6/images/083f17d49152456cbaba076e679afebe5b1f0f59bdea41fcad6565c299d7162c.png)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/83f3baeea7cc4419b9bc0ee9d60b3dc6/images/18b7df87178d4deb9021b455645135c4e5fa8733d2c64c53918214325b2fc196.png)

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/83f3baeea7cc4419b9bc0ee9d60b3dc6/images/143af478c3fa4af69caa277eaa11b645b4647a128cd24c3a830e56df1a555a6a.png)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/83f3baeea7cc4419b9bc0ee9d60b3dc6/images/761d677aec704ee1a693c8572b1990552a7f23f3f9d84dd78440217c4f6dea6c.png)

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/83f3baeea7cc4419b9bc0ee9d60b3dc6/images/ed28a1eead4947d4ad6213cd8e5803c433be9383e98d475f92282a9b125902ec.png)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/83f3baeea7cc4419b9bc0ee9d60b3dc6/images/d7111642477144148d599241dae87612e4.jpg)

# **Why did you decide to use Marvelous Designer? How did it help you serve art direction?**

I chose Marvelous Designer as a tool for creating virtual costumes because it has been developed in this field for many years, the software is very complete, it is the best choice for a CG costume creation tool, through which I can realize the fabric effects I want, and Marvelous Designer has also helped me to broaden my horizons and improve my overall design ability.

# **Can you give us a quick overview of the different tools used in your pipeline?**

Typically in a virtual costume project, I would model the character in C4D, create the costume in Marvelous Designer, UV map it in Photoshop, render it using OC in C4D, and finally post-compose it in Photoshop.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/83f3baeea7cc4419b9bc0ee9d60b3dc6/images/08f7489e33f247bfaa61dd71c13af092a6fa17e1a7a443ad9581511c942c9c4c.jpg)

# **Can you elaborate on the challenges while you’re working on Virtual fashion?**

Since the virtual costumes I wanted to create were very complex, the number of faces needed for the whole project was very high, which caused the computer to become very laggy during the fabric simulation, and in order to solve this problem I had to optimize it by adjusting the settings of each parameter.

# **What tips do you have for other artists using Marvelous Designer?**

I recommend that artists who use Marvelous Designer do a lot of practicing; getting your hands dirty is the fastest way to improve your proficiency with the software, as well as looking at the work of great designers to improve your own aesthetics.

# **How can you describe your overall experience of the use of the Marvelous Designer?**

Easy to use, efficient and convenient to use, very powerful, applicable to a variety of design areas.
content_description: Discover the innovative 3D designs and motion graphics of The Intro, a skilled visual designer specializing in virtual fashion and costume creation using advanced tools like Marvelous Designer.

title: Treasure
content:
## _Meet the experimental story of Alex, a 3D artist and motion designer. Discover how small and simple things found around him transformed into 'TREASURE'._

* * *

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/600785dd8abd466e9124d34d5463fb64/images/fbd59383e6894825952264274f7ec64aTHUMBNAIL.jpg)

# **Interview with Alex Diaconu****|****TREASURE | 3D Artist & Motion Designer**

# **Could you briefly introduce yourself to us?**

Hey everyone! My name is Alex, I'm 31 and I'm a 3D artist and motion designer based in Spain. I've been moving polygons for more than 10 years, It's always been just for fun and I like to keep it that way as much as possible so you could definitely call it my passion. I'm currently spending my time between trying new workflows, personal projects, and freelancing.

# **Let's talk about your recent project, “Treasure”. Can you tell us where you got the inspiration for the concept or what was the visual style you were aiming for?**

I'd love to sit here and talk about having a vision from the very beginning, but this project came to be entirely by mistake and step by step. Some concepts will come to you instantly, some others will develop as you're having fun.

I'm very passionate about experimenting, most of my work comes from experimental processes, which is a trait that comes with being self-taught. The result of said experimentation, and how much fun I'm having doing it, often guides the project at every turn.

This started by deciding to model a couple of things I could see around my desk every day with no goal other than having a good time modeling. The same goes for texturing and lighting, I like doing it so it was simply my pass time.

As I had enough of them a concept was becoming clear, these are the bits I have around me, I was looking at a collection of things I have, simple things but unequivocally mine, my treasure.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/600785dd8abd466e9124d34d5463fb64/images/a0a4ed87f23a404092738dec2252df95613848f32e6c4cdd9962375f44b0addc.jpg)

# **How did you use Marvelous Designer in the artwork?**

I'm by no means an experienced user, so I did what I do best, experiment.

I imported a low poly version of my pile of things as an avatar and generated various "bags" consisting of basic shape and seams.

From there it was just a matter of playing around and generating various iterations until I got folds I like. There lies the fun of simulations.

The second part consisted of setting up another set of simple shapes and seams, and using the pressure feature to basically achieve a "vacuum sealing" rig I could throw any avatar in and simulate.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/600785dd8abd466e9124d34d5463fb64/images/f254a21a511349fe902a832df37f013f2fe5a39e08614b418fe591a25b0ef904.jpg)

# **Why did you decide to use Marvelous Designer? How did it help you serve art direction?**

A work colleague first introduced me to Marvelous. Shout out Fenton if you're reding this!

He is way more interested in character art than I am, nonetheless, I never say no to experimenting with new software and I could immediately see the potential uses and advantages it could have over other solutions.

For me, it's all about results, and natural-looking results are absolutely lovely. Every crease and fold looks so good from the start. I could not imagine having to sculpt this kind of detail, nor getting anything remotely similar from my usual 3D software.

Cloth simulations in most 3D software is still really limited, sluggish, and hardware intensive. Other really powerful tools do not offer an intuitive enough UX to facilitate learning.

I feel like a tool like Marvelous Designer holds the sweet spot, where the GPU simulation is really fast, and is meant for fashion designers it has really intuitive UX to the point where learning how everything works takes little to no time.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/600785dd8abd466e9124d34d5463fb64/images/d46028c30e4341639a62540278838e1e7ec946f0d7584e038df6a6a772c65279.jpg)

# **Can you give us a quick overview of the different tools used in your pipeline?**

Too many to count. Much like my Marvelous Designer use, I like to use dedicated software based on it respective strength.

I use Moi for hard surface modeling, which was the case in this project, ZBrush for sculpting, Decimation Master in ZBrush is really powerful when I need to keep the poly count in check, so it's usually used on high poly Marvelous exports, Octane for physically accurate materials and lighting, World Creator for landscapes, and the list goes on depending on my needs.

Like I said, I think using specialized software for what they're best at is the way to go.

# **Do you have any other projects that you have worked on using Marvelous Designer that you can share with us?**

Of course! I used it for as little as some stickers on my self-portrait, and as much as the centerpiece of my latest project. See below!

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/600785dd8abd466e9124d34d5463fb64/images/05682f09e2294dadb2707600cd5cbc55afe81d17ea3746d2b840abeac8db4992.jpg)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202412/600785dd8abd466e9124d34d5463fb64/images/7ca6b37ced1a42c7b831af6fda9924e3038aedc02dc14c82b81bb84604216231.jpg)

# **How can you describe your overall experience of the use of the Marvelous Designer?**

Overall I'm really pleased, as I mentioned before I found it really user friendly, snappy and fast. I haven't encountered any bugs or crashes even when I push it quite far.

Lastly, thank you for your interest in my work and a message to anyone reading this: Play around and always have fun!

# **_by ALEX DIACONU_**
